title: Josh Radnor discusses "John and Paul: A Love Story in Song" with author Ian Leslie

sentences.en: As a bonus episode for you this week, we are presenting an interview that Josh conducted with Ian Leslie, author of John and Paul, A Love Story and Song,
sentences.zh: 作为本周的加更节目，我们为大家带来了一段访谈，这是乔希对伊恩·莱斯利的采访，伊恩是《约翰与保罗：一个关于爱与歌的故事》一书的作者，

sentences.en: a book that Josh and Craig have talked about several times on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这本书乔希和克雷格在播客里讨论过好几次。

sentences.en: The conversation was originally presented by Barnes & Noble as a live virtual event celebrating the paperback release of the book.
sentences.zh: 这段对话最初由巴诺书店呈现，是一场庆祝该书平装版发售的线上直播活动。

sentences.en: And we've got it here for you right now.
sentences.zh: 现在我们把它带给各位。

sentences.en: I'm Josh Radner.
sentences.zh: 我是乔希·雷德纳。

sentences.en: I'm delighted to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: I'm here with Ian Leslie, the author of John and Paul, A Love Story and Songs, which is a book I just devoured and loved so deeply.
sentences.zh: 我和伊恩·莱斯利在一起，他是《约翰与保罗：一个关于爱与歌的故事》的作者，这本书我刚一口气读完，而且深感喜爱。

sentences.en: I loved it so much.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢它了。

sentences.en: I think I was pretty public about my love of the book.
sentences.zh: 我想我对于自己喜爱这本书的态度一直挺公开的。

sentences.en: So your people tracked me down knowing that I was a fan to do this.
sentences.zh: 所以你们团队知道我是粉丝后，就找到我来做这个访谈。

sentences.en: But welcome.
sentences.zh: 不过欢迎来到这里。

sentences.en: I'm so delighted to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴认识你。

sentences.en: Very nice to meet you, Josh.
sentences.zh: 很高兴认识你，乔希。

sentences.en: And it's really lovely to hear.
sentences.zh: 听到这些真的很开心。

sentences.en: I'm glad my people tracked you down.
sentences.zh: 很高兴我的团队找到了你。

sentences.en: You didn't stand a chance.
sentences.zh: 你根本别无选择。

sentences.en: Well, I always tell people, let people know when you love something.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我总是告诉大家，当你喜欢什么东西时，就要大声说出来。

sentences.en: You know, it's so nice as a maker of things to get that kind of feedback.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，作为创作者，能得到那种反馈感觉真的很棒。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's also, you know, I think it's nice to talk with people who share an enthusiasm for what you've been writing about.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，我也觉得和那些对你所写的内容有着共同热情的人聊天是一件很美好的事。

sentences.en: I will say that I discovered your work because I think like a lot of people, I was it was deep pandemic December 2020, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我得说，我是发现了你的作品，因为我想就像很多人一样，那是疫情深重的2020年12月，如果我没记错的话。

sentences.en: And you wrote a post that went pretty viral called 64 Reasons to Celebrate Paul McCartney.
sentences.zh: 你写了一篇在网上相当火的文章，叫作《致敬保罗·麦卡特尼的64个理由》。

sentences.en: And the starting was after all these years, he's still underrated.
sentences.zh: 开篇写的是，历经这么多年，他依然被低估了。

sentences.en: And I know that for me in that moment, like a lot of people, I was hungering for diversion, but also for inspiration to remember there was a big,
sentences.zh: 我知道对我来说，在那个时刻，就像许多人一样，我渴望着消遣，但也渴望着灵感，去记住外面还有一个巨大、

sentences.en: beautiful world out there of things to love and appreciate and celebrate.
sentences.zh: 美好的世界，里面有那么多值得去爱、去感激和庆祝的事物。

sentences.en: And this post, and for those listening, if you haven't read this, I just reread it today and it's delightful.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章，对于正在收听的各位，如果还没读过的话，我今天又重读了一遍，读起来真的很愉快。

sentences.en: I just I just think it's a wonderful celebration of McCartney.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这是对麦卡特尼的一次美妙致敬。

sentences.en: But I'm curious where the initial impulse to write that post came from.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，当初写那篇文章的最初冲动是从哪来的？

sentences.en: Were you shocked at its virality, how far it traveled and what role that played in leading to your book, John and Paul, Love Story and Songs?
sentences.zh: 你有没有对它的病毒式传播、它传得那么远感到震惊？这在促成你的书《约翰与保罗：一个关于爱与歌的故事》的过程中又起到了什么作用？

sentences.en: Yes, great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，问得好。

sentences.en: And I'm really pleased that you you came across it.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你能读到它。

sentences.en: And that was your kind of route to to the book, because it really that really was the kind of founding moment of John and Paul, a love story and songs.
sentences.zh: 而且那是你接触这本书的途径，因为这确实可以说是《约翰与保罗：一个关于爱与歌的故事》这本书的奠基时刻。

sentences.en: It's it's not about John and Paul.
sentences.zh: 它其实不是关于约翰和保罗的。

sentences.en: It's about Paul.
sentences.zh: 它是关于保罗的。

sentences.en: But it's really kind of it really kind of sparked the book.
sentences.zh: 但它真的算是引发了这本书的创作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Why did I write it?
sentences.zh: 我为什么写它？

sentences.en: I mean, like a lot of people, not everyone.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，像很多人一样，虽然不是所有人。

sentences.en: But like a lot of people, I had time on my hands in the in the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但像很多人一样，我在疫情期间有很多空闲时间。

sentences.en: And I thought, well, I'm going to write this ridiculously long article I kind of have in my head about why Paul McCartney is really good at music.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，我要写一篇荒谬的长文，关于我脑海里一直在想的为什么保罗·麦卡特尼音乐素养这么高。

sentences.en: And I'm not, you know, no magazine is going to buy this, but I've got a substat called The Ruffian and I can publish what the hell I want.
sentences.zh: 而且我知道，没有哪家杂志会买单，但我有一个叫《鲁菲恩》的子堆栈专栏，我可以随心所欲地发布我想发的东西。

sentences.en: And so I I've been thinking about it and actually writing notes about it for years because I just had this really strong feeling that we don't appreciate what an immense genius Paul McCartney is,
sentences.zh: 所以多年来我一直在思考这个问题，甚至一直在做笔记，因为我有一种非常强烈的直觉，那就是我们没有充分认识到保罗·麦卡特尼是多么巨大的天才，

sentences.en: you know, partly because he's still with us.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是他仍然和我们在一起。

sentences.en: So we're just like, oh, yeah, it's just Paul McCartney or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只会觉得，哦，对啊，不就是保罗·麦卡特尼嘛之类的。

sentences.en: And it's like, no, no, no, guys, this guy is, you know, this is an incredible genius in our midst and we should be grateful and appreciate him.
sentences.zh: 而事实是，不，不，不，伙计们，这家伙，你知道的，这是我们当中不可思议的天才，我们应该心存感激并去欣赏他。

sentences.en: So I wrote this long post and I yeah, I didn't expect it to many people to read it, apart from a few hardcore kind of fans.
sentences.zh: 所以我写了这篇长文，而且我确实没想到会有那么多人读它，除了少数死忠粉之外。

sentences.en: But it went insanely viral and hundreds of thousands of people read it around the world.
sentences.zh: 但它疯狂地火了，全世界有几十万人阅读了它。

sentences.en: And it was also very emotional response.
sentences.zh: 而且这也引起了非常感性的反响。

sentences.en: So people were as you seem to have been right.
sentences.zh: 所以人们正如你当初表现的那样，对吧？

sentences.en: People were very touched by it.
sentences.zh: 人们被它深深地触动了。

sentences.en: And up until then.
sentences.zh: 直到那个时候。

sentences.en: The idea of writing a Beatles book hadn't really been on the agenda for me.
sentences.zh: 写一本关于披头士乐队的书，其实并不在我的计划之内。

sentences.en: I'd written books, you know, but generally my books have been about psychology and, you know, the trait of curiosity.
sentences.zh: 我写过书，你知道的，但我的书通常都是关于心理学的，你知道的，也就是好奇心这种特质。

sentences.en: Or or the conflict and disagreement.
sentences.zh: 或者说关于冲突与分歧。

sentences.en: I don't really write about music, but obviously I love music and I've loved the Beatles since I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 我其实不怎么写关于音乐的文章，但显然我热爱音乐，而且我从小就喜欢披头士。

sentences.en: But I didn't really feel licensed to write a book about the Beatles.
sentences.zh: 但我真的觉得自己没有获得许可去写一本关于披头士的书。

sentences.en: And what happened when this post went viral and so many people told me how much they loved it, including some very serious music writers.
sentences.zh: 而当这篇文章在网上疯传，有那么多人告诉我他们有多喜欢它，其中还包括一些非常严肃的音乐作家时，发生了什么呢？

sentences.en: I suddenly thought, oh, wow, maybe I could.
sentences.zh: 我突然想，哦，哇，也许我可以。

sentences.en: Maybe I could write a book about the group that I'd loved since I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以写一本关于我从小就热爱的这个乐队的书。

sentences.en: And the moment I started thinking that, the moment I sort of realized that was a possibility, I thought, well, if I'm going to do that, it's going to be about John and Paul.
sentences.zh: 就在我开始有这个想法的那个瞬间，当我某种程度上意识到这是一种可能时，我想，好吧，如果我要这么做，那它一定是要关于约翰和保罗的。

sentences.en: I mean, I knew that that was the thing that I really wanted to write a book about.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我很清楚这正是我真正想写书的题材。

sentences.en: In fact, when I was writing the Paul McCartney post, I took some of the John and Paul material out because it was already too long.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我在写保罗·麦卡特尼的那篇帖子时，我删掉了一些关于约翰和保罗的素材，因为篇幅已经太长了。

sentences.en: And I thought, oh, my God, if I get into this, it's going to be another 10,000 words.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，哦，天哪，如果我深入挖掘这个，又得凭空多出一万字。

sentences.en: So I've got to cut that.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须把那部分删掉。

sentences.en: But yeah, so I sort of knew right away that that's the thing I'm most fascinated by, this just inexhaustible fascination of this complex, mysterious,
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，我基本上立刻就明白这正是我最着迷的东西，这种对他们两个年轻男人之间错综复杂、神秘莫测、

sentences.en: deep and very moving relationship between these two young men.
sentences.zh: 深厚且极为感人的关系永无止境的着迷。

sentences.en: Do you feel that because you're not a music writer by trade, was there some liberation in that?
sentences.zh: 你觉得因为你不是专职音乐作家，这其中是不是有一种解放感？

sentences.en: Did you feel that you weren't beholden to certain music journalist tropes that you could just give it your own kind of fans perspective?
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得你没有受到某些音乐记者陈词滥调的束缚，从而可以展现出你自己的某种粉丝视角？

sentences.en: Yes, I think that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得完全是这样。

sentences.en: I think that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 我觉得完全是这样。

sentences.en: I came to it as a bit of an outsider to music journalism, to the tradition of writing about the Beatles, to even to Beatles fandom in a way.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，我对音乐新闻界、对披头士乐队的写作传统、甚至对披头士的粉丝群体来说，都有点像是个局外人。

sentences.en: Like, I'm not totally inside the kind of online Beatles world.
sentences.zh: 就像我并不是完全身处那种网络披头士世界的核心。

sentences.en: I mean, I read a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我读过很多这方面的东西。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢。

sentences.en: But it's not really kind of my thing in particular.
sentences.zh: 但这其实并不算是我特别专注的领域。

sentences.en: So I'm a sort of partial outsider in more ways than one.
sentences.zh: 所以我从多方面来看算是一个局外人。

sentences.en: And I think that did really help me kind of write a fresh narrative and a fresh story, because I was always coming to all these stories and narratives and just thinking,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这确实帮我写出了一种全新的叙事和全新的故事，因为我每次接触所有这些故事和叙述时，都会想：

sentences.en: is that really the way I think about it?
sentences.zh: 这真的是我所认为的那样吗？

sentences.en: And often it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 而通常情况并非如此。

sentences.en: So I think that was helpful.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这很有帮助。

sentences.en: And in a way, it sort of mirrors the relationship of the Beatles to rock and roll, to American music.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，它在某种程度上反映了披头士乐队与摇滚乐、与美国音乐的关系。

sentences.en: You know, they absolutely loved it, but they were also they had this kind of natural distance from it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们绝对热爱这些音乐，但同时他们与这些音乐保持着一种天然的距离。

sentences.en: And they were kind of looking at it from from a different a different angle.
sentences.zh: 他们是以一种不同的、全新的视角在看待这一切。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: One thing I got very strongly from your article.
sentences.zh: 我从你的文章中强烈感受到了这一点。

sentences.en: Well, when I was reading it, I realized and I never said this out loud, but I was like, oh, I'm a Paul guy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我读它的时候，我意识到——虽然我从没大声说过，但当时我在想，哦，我是一个保罗迷。

sentences.en: And I had a roommate in college who was a real John guy.
sentences.zh: 我在大学里有个室友，他是个彻头彻尾的约翰迷。

sentences.en: And he was he was kind of an heir to the tradition.
sentences.zh: 他可以说是那种传统的继承者。

sentences.en: And you talk about this in both the book and the article that after, you know, post Beatles,
sentences.zh: 你在书和文章中都谈到了这一点，那就是在你知道的披头士解散之后，

sentences.en: Lennon and Jan Wenner and all these different journalists kind of created this myth around Lennon as the singular genius of the Beatles.
sentences.zh: 列侬、扬·韦纳和各种各样的记者围绕列侬塑造了这样一种神话，把他描绘成披头士乐队中独一无二的天才。

sentences.en: And Paul was this kind of lightweight tunesmith.
sentences.zh: 而保罗则被描绘成那种无足轻重的曲调匠人。

sentences.en: And after Lennon died, that myth got even more kind of calcified in the collective conscience.
sentences.zh: 在列侬去世后，这种神话在集体意识中变得更加根深蒂固。

sentences.en: But it seems to me that your your your work around this stuff, even though the book is really about John and Paul,
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，你围绕这些内容展开的作品——尽管这本书实际上是关于约翰和保罗的——

sentences.en: it's a bit of a rehabilitation project for Paul on certain in certain ways that that to claim that one was the great genius.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上可以说是一次为保罗进行的名誉恢复工程，以打破那种断言某一个人才是伟大天才的说法。

sentences.en: I mean, like they were they had a deeply symbiotic relationship and the Beatles that we love was four, but it was also really two.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们之间存在着一种极其深厚的共生关系，我们所热爱的披头士虽然有四个人，但实际上也是两个人。

sentences.en: And I just love that you kind of balanced the scales on that.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢你在这方面重新端平了天平。

sentences.en: Was that a big was that big in your mind as you were writing the book?
sentences.zh: 在你写这本书的时候，这在你的脑海中占据了很大的分量吗？

sentences.en: Yes, to some extent.
sentences.zh: 是的，在某种程度上是的。

sentences.en: And I didn't want it to just be, you know, his Paul side of the story, because I wanted to portray what you just described as a deeply symbiotic relationship.
sentences.zh: 而且我不想让它仅仅变成保罗视角的那个故事，因为我想刻画你刚刚所描述的那种极其深厚的共生关系。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: To show how they each created the other.
sentences.zh: 为了展示他们是如何彼此成就的。

sentences.en: And I also wanted to kind of get away from the stereotypes of both in the popular imagination.
sentences.zh: 而且我也想跳出大众想象中对两人的各种刻板印象。

sentences.en: But certainly you're right that the one that the person whose reputation has suffered more from this caricature is Paul.
sentences.zh: 但你的确说得对，在这场刻板塑造中，受声誉损害更严重的人其实是保罗。

sentences.en: And to some extent, I was kind of making up for that.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，我这也是在弥补这一点。

sentences.en: But of course, I wasn't the only one.
sentences.zh: 不过当然，我并不是唯一这么做的人。

sentences.en: In fact, you know, you can see his rehabilitation going on in various different ways.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道的，你可以看到大家正以各种不同的方式为他平反。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Peter Jackson's get get back movie.
sentences.zh: 比如彼得·杰克逊的《回归》纪录片。

sentences.en: So in a way, I was just part of the general kind of revaluing of Paul.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，我只是顺应了大众重新评估保罗的潮流。

sentences.en: I think this gone on in the last few years, but I'm definitely proud to be a part of it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这股风潮在过去几年一直在持续，而我也绝对为能参与其中感到自豪。

sentences.en: But my other challenge was, you know, my related challenge here was as basically a Paul guy, you know, since I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 但我的另一个挑战是，我在这方面面临的相关挑战是，从小到大我基本上就是个“保罗派”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Like, how am I going to bring John Lennon to life sufficiently that a John Lennon fan is is is not going to read this and go, oh, well, he's not very nice to John.
sentences.zh: 比如，我要怎么才能把约翰·列侬刻画得足够生动，才不会让一个约翰·列侬的粉丝读到这里时觉得，“哦，好吧，他对约翰可不太好”。

sentences.en: And so I kind of consciously made myself fall in love a bit with John, you know, and that involved talking to people who really love him, who see him as a real, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我会有意识地让自己稍微爱上约翰，你知道的，这包括去和那些真正爱他的人交流，在他们眼中，他是一个真正的……

sentences.en: as he is as a musical genius.
sentences.zh: 一个真正的音乐天才。

sentences.en: But like, help me understand what made him special, why he's and and just try to look at him from that way as a person and a musician.
sentences.zh: 但是，帮我理解是什么造就了他的特殊，为什么他是这样的，然后试着从那种角度去看待他，把他当成一个人和一个音乐家。

sentences.en: And I got there, you know, so in the end, like, I'm still a poor guy, but I love John more than I did before.
sentences.zh: 我做到了，所以最后，虽然我还是个保罗迷，但我比以前更爱约翰了。

sentences.en: And I see them both certainly as more.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实把他们俩看作是……

sentences.en: Yeah, it's different and more complex than than than cartoons.
sentences.zh: 对，这比那些扁平的漫画形象要丰富得多，也复杂得多。

sentences.en: One of the delights of reading this book, because you maybe maybe you can describe in broad strokes, like one,
sentences.zh: 阅读这本书的一大乐趣在于——也许你可以大致描述一下——首先，

sentences.en: like what this book is and also how you maybe how you kind of pitched it, you know, to publishers.
sentences.zh: 比如这本书到底是关于什么的，还有你是怎么把这个构思推销给出版商的。

sentences.en: But one of the delights for me is each section of their, you know, friendship.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，乐趣之一在于他们友谊的每一个阶段。

sentences.en: And there's a song that goes along where you're showing how their friendships affect the music and the music affect the friendship.
sentences.zh: 书中会配上一首歌，展示他们的友谊如何影响音乐，而音乐又如何影响他们的友谊。

sentences.en: And it's it's really delightful.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常美妙。

sentences.en: I knew most of the songs, but some of them I didn't know.
sentences.zh: 大部分歌我都听过，但也有一些是我不知道的。

sentences.en: So so you put the song on either before or after the chapter that you're reading.
sentences.zh: 所以你会把这首歌放在你所阅读的章节之前或之后。

sentences.en: And there was there was great joy in that.
sentences.zh: 这其中有着极大的乐趣。

sentences.en: But I'm just curious, like how you speak about this book in broad strokes, like how you kind of describe it.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，你是如何大致谈论这本书的，比如你会怎么形容它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So and yeah, so let's go back to that moment where I was thinking, OK, well, I could I could write a book about the Beatles.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，让我们回到那个时刻，当时我在想，好吧，我可以写一本关于披头士乐队的书。

sentences.en: And the thing I'm most interested in is the chemistry between these two young kind of damaged, brilliant young men who meet and essentially just lock into each other.
sentences.zh: 而我最感兴趣的是这两个年轻、带点破碎感却又才华横溢的年轻人之间的化学反应，他们相遇了，基本上就像磁铁一样紧紧吸引在一起。

sentences.en: And it is kind of a love story.
sentences.zh: 这确实有点像一个爱情故事。

sentences.en: It's almost like love, love at first sight.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像是一见钟情。

sentences.en: And then they go on to have this kind of tender, loving, admiring, but also conflicted and jealousy ridden and sometimes sort of unpleasant, you know, relationship.
sentences.zh: 然后他们便拥有了这种既温柔、充满爱意又互相欣赏，但同时也充满矛盾、嫉妒交织，有时甚至有点令人不快的关系。

sentences.en: But they never really lose that, that they never lose that bond.
sentences.zh: 但他们从未真正失去那种羁绊。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And and the more I thought about it, the more I thought that that kind of is a central thread, you know, maybe even the central thread in the story of the Beatles.
sentences.zh: 而且我越是思考，就越觉得这算是一条核心线索，甚至可以说是披头士乐队故事中的核心线索。

sentences.en: They are kind of a group within a group, these two, you know, even people, even George and Ringo would say, you know, there was us and then there was John and Paul kind of.
sentences.zh: 他们俩其实是团队中的一个小圈子，甚至连乔治和林戈都会说，你知道的，除了我们之外，还有约翰和保罗。

sentences.en: And of course, they were the primary songwriters and kind of the most dominant personalities in the group.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们俩是主要的词曲创作者，也是组合中最具统治力的人物。

sentences.en: And George and Ringo's contributions are immense and indispensable.
sentences.zh: 乔治和林戈的贡献是巨大且不可或缺的。

sentences.en: I'm not putting, you know, I don't want to marginalize them, but but but absolutely, John and Paul were the kind of engine at the heart of it.
sentences.zh: 我并不是要边缘化他们，但毫无疑问，约翰和保罗才是整支乐队的核心引擎。

sentences.en: And so I thought, OK, first of all, have there been any books about John and Paul?
sentences.zh: 所以我想，好吧，首先，以前有没有人写过关于约翰和保罗的书？

sentences.en: Turns out, no, it's like, no, I mean, might have been one or two that I've missed.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，没有。我是说，也许有一两本我漏掉了。

sentences.en: But like, in terms of major, significant books, no.
sentences.zh: 但就那种重磅的、具有重要意义的书籍而言，确实没有。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's been group biographies of all four of them.
sentences.zh: 市面上有关于他们四人全体的传记。

sentences.en: There have been books about the individual Beatles.
sentences.zh: 也有关于披头士单飞成员的书。

sentences.en: And then there were thousands of books about different slices of the story.
sentences.zh: 还有成千上万本讲述这个故事不同切面的书。

sentences.en: But there's no one book about the Leonard McCartney relationship.
sentences.zh: 但就是没有一本专门讲述列侬与麦卡特尼关系的图书。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So immediately I thought, well, this is crazy.
sentences.zh: 所以当时我立刻就想，嗯，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And it seemed like an open goal, as we say, in football or soccer.
sentences.zh: 而且正如我们在足球或英式足球中所说的那样，这简直是一个大好的机会。

sentences.en: So I thought, you know, that that encouraged me.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，你知道的，这给了我很大的鼓励。

sentences.en: And then I knew pretty much from the beginning that if I was going to tell the story, I would tell it through the songs because.
sentences.zh: 从一开始我就很清楚，如果我要讲这个故事，我会通过他们的歌曲来讲述，因为……

sentences.en: I don't I don't think you can understand the music of the Beatles without understanding the developing, evolving chemistry of this friendship, this very intense friendship,
sentences.zh: 我不认为——我不认为如果不理解这种友谊的发展和不断演变的化学反应——这种非常深厚的友谊，

sentences.en: this romance, effectively.
sentences.zh: 这段罗曼史，实际上，

sentences.en: And conversely, I don't think you can understand the complexity of that relationship without looking at it through the music, because these guys thought and felt in songs.
sentences.zh: 你就无法理解披头士乐队的音乐；反过来也是一样，如果不通过音乐来审视这段关系的复杂性，你同样无法理解它，因为这些家伙是用歌曲来思考和感受的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So much of their emotional life was tied up in making songs, in writing songs, in singing with each other.
sentences.zh: 他们的大部分情感生活都与创作歌曲、写歌以及彼此对唱息息相关。

sentences.en: They weren't particularly emotionally articulate with each other and with others, but they were they were incredibly emotional in their music.
sentences.zh: 他们彼此之间以及对别人并不是特别擅长用语言表达情感，但他们的音乐却蕴含着不可思议的情感。

sentences.en: And so I just thought to understand the emotional power of the Beatles, you have to go back to the relationship and to understand the relationship, you have to go to music.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，要理解披头士乐队的情感力量，你必须追溯到他们的关系上；而要理解他们的关系，你必须走进他们的音乐。

sentences.en: So it's like, well,
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比，

sentences.en: I'll just tell the narrative is effectively a biography of the relationship where I start from when they meet in 1957 and I go right through to the end of the friendship,
sentences.zh: 我将要讲述的叙事实际上就是这段关系的传记，我从他们1957年相遇开始讲起，一直讲到这段友谊的结束，

sentences.en: which is obviously John's death in 1980.
sentences.zh: 也就是约翰在1980年去世的那一刻。

sentences.en: And I tell the whole thing through through the music that they're making and that kind of scheme, that plan for the book kind of came very quickly, which doesn't often happen.
sentences.zh: 我通过他们创作的音乐来讲述整个故事，这种构思、这种对这本书的规划很快就成型了，这在平时并不常见。

sentences.en: And that was effectively the book that I wrote.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上就是我写出来的这本书。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Were you I mean, it's an amazing thing to find a lane in Beatles scholarship that hasn't been trod.
sentences.zh: 你是说——在披头士的研究领域中找到一条未曾涉足的道路，这真是一件了不起的事。

sentences.en: You know, you know, that you actually found this thing and it was shocking to you that it hadn't been explored.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你居然找到了这个切入点，而且令你震惊的是，这个方向竟然从未被开发过。

sentences.en: How much I imagine you there's kind of a trick you would have to do.
sentences.zh: 我能想象你当时不得不进行某种技巧性的处理，有多大程度……

sentences.en: I'm making this up as I go.
sentences.zh: 我这是现编的。

sentences.en: But this idea of you have all this knowledge of the Beatles in a lifetime of loving the Beatles.
sentences.zh: 但这种想法是，你拥有关于披头士的所有知识，你用了一生去爱披头士。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you have to approach it with this kind of beginner's mind.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你又必须以一种“初学者之心”来对待它。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Also excavate.
sentences.zh: 还要去发掘。

sentences.en: You're a researcher.
sentences.zh: 你是一名研究员。

sentences.en: You're a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 你是一名记者。

sentences.en: So I'm curious how you thread the needle between those two things and what shocked and and surprised you as you went that you discovered in addition to, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇你是如何在这两者之间找到平衡的，以及在你深入的过程中，除了重新爱上约翰之外，还有什么让你感到震惊和惊喜的发现，你知道的，

sentences.en: falling back in love with John.
sentences.zh: 重新爱上约翰。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Great question.
sentences.zh: 好问题。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't think I'm not sure that like there was massive shocks and revelations and I didn't expect there to be, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不认为——我不确定是否曾有过什么巨大的冲击和启示，而且我也没指望会有，你知道的，

sentences.en: like they're the most sort of studied and covered and filmed and recorded and written about group and people in history.
sentences.zh: 毕竟他们是历史上被研究最多、被报道最多、被拍摄最多、被记录最多、被书写最多的乐队和群体。

sentences.en: So the challenge for me was never going to be like, oh, can I turn up some new revelation?
sentences.zh: 所以对我的挑战从来都不是：“噢，我能不能挖出什么新的猛料？”

sentences.en: I just I mean, there might be from from other people, but it wasn't something I was going to do.
sentences.zh: 我是说——别人或许能挖出来，但这并不是我要做的事。

sentences.en: It's not something I was going to I was not going to go through archives or I didn't do interviews and so on.
sentences.zh: 这不是我会去做的方式，我不会去翻阅档案馆，也没有去做采访之类的。

sentences.en: It was more like, let's take all the information that's out there and let me find my story, you know, my version of events.
sentences.zh: 更像是，让我们把现有的所有信息汇集起来，然后由我来寻找我的故事，也就是我版本的事件经过。

sentences.en: I don't claim to be a scholar laying down the official great story of the Beatles.
sentences.zh: 我并不自诩是一个奠定披头士官方伟大故事的学者。

sentences.en: I'm like, this is the way I see it, guys.
sentences.zh: 我的态度是：伙计们，这就是我眼中的他们。

sentences.en: And and then you're right.
sentences.zh: 然后你说得对。

sentences.en: I had to have this kind of beginner's mind where I'm relying on a lot of other sources, effectively.
sentences.zh: 我必须保持这种“初学者之心”，实际上，我要依赖大量的其他来源。

sentences.en: Well, there's always the primary sources.
sentences.zh: 嗯，总是有第一手资料的。

sentences.en: You can go to interviews with them.
sentences.zh: 你可以去读他们的采访。

sentences.en: You can watch them.
sentences.zh: 你可以看他们的影像。

sentences.en: You can watch, you know, you can listen to the music.
sentences.zh: 你可以看，你知道的，你可以听他们的音乐。

sentences.en: But there's also lots of secondary sources.
sentences.zh: 但也有很多第二手资料。

sentences.en: And when I'm reading those secondary sources, I'm thinking,
sentences.zh: 而当我阅读这些第二手资料时，我在想，

sentences.en: OK, how much of this do I actually believe?
sentences.zh: 好吧，这里面有多少是我真正相信的？

sentences.en: How much of this story that they're telling do I buy?
sentences.zh: 他们讲述的这个故事，我有多少是买账的？

sentences.en: And what am I going to bring to it?
sentences.zh: 那我能给它带来什么呢？

sentences.en: Because the last thing I wanted to do was retell the same old stories,
sentences.zh: 因为我最不想做的事，就是去复述那些陈旧的老故事，

sentences.en: which, frankly, a lot of Beatles journalism and a lot of Beatles authors do, you know, even in part,
sentences.zh: 说实话，很多披头士的报道和作者都在这么做，你知道的，哪怕只是部分地，

sentences.en: even when they're writing something different, part of the book will be, oh, yeah, I know this bit.
sentences.zh: 甚至当他们在写一些不同的东西时，书的一部分也会是，哦，对啊，这段我知道。

sentences.en: I know this bit.
sentences.zh: 这段我知道。

sentences.en: I wanted every page of it to feel fresh in some way.
sentences.zh: 我希望它的每一页在某种程度上都让人觉得耳目一新。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And and and that meant, yeah, kind of just looking at everything, as you say, with with with fresh eyes.
sentences.zh: 而且这意味着，是的，就像你说的，用一种全新的眼光去审视一切。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think there's been I think taking your book along with the Peter Jackson film there,
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得，结合你的书和彼得·杰克逊的那部电影，

sentences.en: I think that the Beatles in the popular imagination, you think of like Shea Stadium, you think of Beatlemania.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在大众的想象中，说到披头士，你会想到谢伊体育场，会想到披头士狂热。

sentences.en: You there's this kind of like epic, grand, big mythic story that involves fans and critics and 60s and drugs.
sentences.zh: 你会有一种史诗般宏大、充满神话色彩的故事感，里面有歌迷、评论家、20世纪60年代和药物。

sentences.en: And it's just this big, big, big thing.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个非常非常宏大的东西。

sentences.en: And what I felt both watching the Peter Jackson documentary and reading your book,
sentences.zh: 而我无论是看彼得·杰克逊的纪录片还是读你的书时所感受到的是，

sentences.en: to me, the singular kind of image is them either on LSD or not on LSD, but staring into each other's eyes for as long as they could for hours.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，最独特的画面就是他们不管是嗑了LSD还是没嗑，却尽可能长时间地、几个小时地凝视着彼此的眼睛。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, just intensely trying to connect.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那种极其专注地想要建立连接的努力。

sentences.en: And it almost feels like you took the macro and you brought it as small as it could go, which is like to their eyeballs.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像是你把宏观的视野缩小到了极致，缩到了他们的眼珠子上。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's beautifully put.
sentences.zh: 这话讲得太妙了。

sentences.en: It's beautifully put.
sentences.zh: 这话讲得真妙。

sentences.en: And it was definitely like a central aim of the book was to convey the emotional intimacy of of the relationship.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是本书的核心目标之一，即传达他们之间那种情感上的亲密关系。

sentences.en: And I wanted it to be an emotional book.
sentences.zh: 而且我希望这是一本充满情感的书。

sentences.en: You know, lots of Beatles books are really fascinating, fun to read, amusing, factually dense.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，很多披头士的书都非常迷人、读起来有趣、好玩、事实密集。

sentences.en: But there aren't very many of them that really move me.
sentences.zh: 但其中真正能打动我的并不多。

sentences.en: And that's odd because it's an incredibly moving story.
sentences.zh: 这很奇怪，因为这是一个极其感人的故事。

sentences.en: And the music, of course, is incredibly moving and emotionally powerful because it comes from these emotional guys.
sentences.zh: 而且音乐当然也是极其感人和充满情感力量的，因为它们出自这些多愁善感的家伙之手。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so I wanted to kind of, yeah, tell the story in a way that that that touched people and moved people and made them laugh, made them cry,
sentences.zh: 所以我想，是的，以一种能触动人、打动人、让他们又笑又哭的方式来讲这个故事，

sentences.en: because that's what the story does does to me.
sentences.zh: 因为这个故事对我就是这样的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that's that's right at the heart of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这正是核心所在。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And there's a kind of to do that, I think you have to dust off a lot.
sentences.zh: 而且为了做到这一点，我觉得你必须掸掉很多尘埃。

sentences.en: You kind of have to demythologize these people.
sentences.zh: 你得把这些人祛魅。

sentences.en: You have to remove them from the rock Mount Olympus and and really get to the heart of they were teenage boys who'd both lost their mothers,
sentences.zh: 你得把他们从摇滚奥林匹斯山上请下来，真正触及他们的核心——他们其实是两个都失去了母亲的少年，

sentences.en: which is a central kind of psychological.
sentences.zh: 这是一种核心的心理状态。

sentences.en: You know, you go pretty deep into that, that they found each other at this very tender moment in their lives and they saved each other.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你对此作了相当深入的探讨，他们在生命中这个非常敏感的时刻遇到了彼此，并且拯救了彼此。

sentences.en: I mean, they could have been, you know, fallen into delinquency, but instead they fell into each other.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们本可能会误入歧途，但相反，他们坠入了彼此的“爱河”。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 对，完全是这样。

sentences.en: And, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，

sentences.en: a lot of the accounts and the way people kind of written have written about or talked about the Beatles and Leonard McCartney specifically were not satisfying to me because they would say things like,
sentences.zh: 很多关于披头士、特别是约翰和保罗的叙述和评论并不能让我满意，因为他们会说一些诸如……的话，

sentences.en: you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: well, obviously they were great mates or they were like brothers, you know, and I was I was thinking, well, they're nothing like the mates that I have.
sentences.zh: “哦，很明显他们是很好的哥们儿”或者“他们就像亲兄弟一样”，你知道的，当时我就在想，这跟我认识的哥们儿完全不一样。

sentences.en: You know, I don't have friends like this and I don't like my relationship with my brother is nothing like the relationship.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我没有这样的朋友，而且我和我兄弟的关系也跟这种关系完全不一样。

sentences.en: I have a good relationship with my brother, but it's nothing like John and Paul.
sentences.zh: 我和我兄弟关系很好，但这跟约翰和保罗完全不同。

sentences.en: And and then there were some people, you know, there's a minority people of real Beatles, you know, some Beatles fans are like, well,
sentences.zh: 然后还有一些人，你知道的，极少数真正的披头士粉丝会觉得，

sentences.en: I think they were secretly homosexual and so on.
sentences.zh: “我觉得他们俩私下是同性恋”诸如此类的。

sentences.en: I never believed that either.
sentences.zh: 我从来不信这个。

sentences.en: I felt like people kept trying to put them into these boxes, basically, you know, like, oh, they were friends or they were like brothers.
sentences.zh: 我觉得人们总是试图把他们塞进这些框框里，基本上就是这样，你知道的，比如“哦，他们就是朋友”或者“他们就像兄弟”。

sentences.en: They were gay, right, because those are the boxes that we have for male relationships.
sentences.zh: 他们是同性恋，对吧，因为这就是我们对男性关系的理解。

sentences.en: But there's something about their relationship, their chemistry, which doesn't fit into our usual categories.
sentences.zh: 但他们的关系、他们的化学反应，有一种说不清道不明的东西，不符合我们常规的分类。

sentences.en: And that was kind of skewing the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 这有点扭曲了整件事。

sentences.en: And that's why you end up with these kind of distorted versions of them, because people didn't quite weren't kind of get trying to get to the heart of that.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你最终会看到这种他们被扭曲的形象，因为人们并没有真正试图去触及核心。
